title: Chapter 11 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Docker security essentials: namespaces, capabilities, rootless mode, runtime hardening, and image trust!

questions.question: Which Linux kernel feature provides process isolation so a container sees only its own processes?
questions.explanation: PID namespace isolates the process ID number space.

questions.question: By default, Docker containers run with full root privileges on the host.
questions.explanation: Even when running as root inside the container, capabilities are limited and namespaces isolate the container.

questions.question: What are Linux capabilities used for in Docker?
options: To define CPU and memory limits
To split the traditional root privileges into smaller, assignable units
questions.explanation: Capabilities allow granting specific powers (like binding to low ports) without full root.

questions.question: What does `--cap-drop ALL` do?
options: Removes all capabilities from the container
Runs the container as a non‑root user
questions.explanation: It starts the container with no capabilities. You then add back only needed ones with `--cap-add`.

questions.question: Rootless Docker runs the Docker daemon and containers without any root privileges on the host.
questions.explanation: Rootless mode uses user namespaces and other techniques to run entirely as a non‑root user.

questions.question: What is a limitation of rootless Docker regarding networking?
options: It cannot bind to ports below 1024 by default
It requires a separate network plugin
It does not support overlay networks
questions.explanation: Because the daemon runs without root, binding to privileged ports (<1024) requires system configuration.

questions.question: The `--read-only` flag makes the container’s root filesystem ________.
questions.explanation: It mounts the root filesystem in read‑only mode.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `--tmpfs /tmp` when combined with `--read-only`?
options: To provide a writable temporary filesystem for paths that need write access
questions.explanation: Some applications expect writable directories like /tmp; tmpfs provides an in‑memory writable space.

questions.question: What does `--security-opt no-new-privileges` prevent?
options: Setuid binaries from granting additional privileges
questions.explanation: It sets the `no_new_privs` flag, blocking privilege escalation via setuid executables.

questions.question: What is Docker Content Trust?
options: A system for signing and verifying images using digital signatures
questions.explanation: Content Trust uses Notary to sign images and verify publishers.

questions.question: With Docker Content Trust enabled, you can still pull unsigned images.
questions.explanation: DCT will refuse to pull images that are not signed or whose signatures cannot be verified.

questions.question: Which tool can scan a Docker image for known vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: Trivy is a popular open‑source vulnerability scanner for container images.

questions.question: Why should vulnerability scanning be part of your CI pipeline?
options: To prevent deploying images with known critical vulnerabilities
questions.explanation: Shifting left catches issues before they reach production.

questions.question: Docker's default seccomp profile allows all system calls.
questions.explanation: The default profile blocks around 44 syscalls to reduce the attack surface.

questions.question: Which command would you use to run a container with the most restrictive capabilities?
questions.explanation: Dropping all and adding back only the needed capability follows the least privilege principle.

questions.question: What does Docker Scout provide?
options: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) and vulnerability insights
questions.explanation: Docker Scout helps with SBOM generation and vulnerability analysis.

questions.question: You can apply AppArmor or SELinux profiles to containers using the `--security-opt` flag.
questions.explanation: Yes, `--security-opt apparmor=profile` or `--security-opt label=type:...`

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Linux namespace used by Docker?
questions.explanation: Docker uses PID, network, mount, UTS, IPC, and user namespaces. 'Database' is not a namespace.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of user namespaces (userns-remap) in Docker?
options: It maps the container’s root to a non‑root user on the host, reducing breakout impact
questions.explanation: User namespaces remap UIDs, so even if a process escapes, it has limited host privileges.

questions.question: To enable Docker Content Trust for a single session, you can `export ________=1`.
questions.explanation: Setting this environment variable activates content trust enforcement.
